descriptionChirho: The feminine noun חִתִּית meaning 'terror, dread,' used exclusively in Ezekiel's oracles against the nations (Ezek 26:17; 32:23-32). Denotes the terror or dread that mighty warriors and kingdoms inspired among the living during their lifetime, now contrasted with their descent to Sheol. Appears with various pronominal suffixes: חִתִּיתָם 'their terror' (Ezek 26:17; 32:24-26, 30), חִתִּיתוֹ/חִתִּיתִי 'his/my terror' (Ezek 32:32, Ketiv/Qere variant), and in construct חִתִּית 'terror of' (Ezek 32:23, 27). The Ketiv [חתיתו] and Qere (חִתִּיתִי) at Ezek 32:32 are text-critical variants of the same word, not different senses. Multilingual evidence is uniform: Arabic رُعْبَ/رُعْبِ (terror/dread), German Entsetzen (terror), Korean 공포 (terror), Spanish terror, Hindi भय (fear), French terreur (terror).
